title: Locally Profinite Groups And Pro-Order
body_html:
Locally Profinite Groups And Pro-Order

A topological group $G$ is locally profinite if it has a basis of neighborhoods of the identity made of open compact subgroups.

For a compact open subgroup $K\subset G$, its pro-order $|K|$ is the least common multiple, in the sense of supernatural numbers, of the orders of the finite quotients of $K$.

The pro-order of $G$ is

$$ |G|:=\operatorname{lcm}_{K\subset G\text{ compact open}} |K|. $$

The draft writes a supernatural number as a function on primes and decomposes

$$ |G|=|G|_f |G|_\infty, $$

where $|G|_f$ and $|G|_\infty$ have disjoint supports. The greatest common divisor of supernatural numbers is denoted by $\wedge$.

Draft Caution

This node records the convention used by the current TeX draft. It does not attempt to prove the supernatural-number formalism or its functorial properties.
